messages:
alex: Heads-up — nightly CI flagged a memory spike on `nightly-run-gpu-32` for the `model-optim` branch, several OOMs starting ~01:10 UTC. Not sure if this is allocator-related or a KV-cache growth.
ci-bot: [ALERT] job nightly-run-gpu-32 failed (OOM). Logs: https://ci.example/12345, artifacts: https://ci.example/artifacts/12345. Re-run: `./ci/retry 12345` :warning:

maria: thanks, grabbing logs now. any recent merges to runtime or allocator in the last 24h?

sam: @maria I merged allocator opt (GH: #678) ~18h ago — it touched pooling/hugebuf paths. I ran local stress but didn't see OOMs.

kevin: I see repeated growth in resident set in the logs around the token 180->220 window. attaching a snippet from the tail: `RSS: 42GB -> 68GB in 30s` — looks like something not freeing KV or a temp buffer.

jen: i can try repro on a small node with a reduced seq length and same workload. which command should i use?

alex: try `./scripts/ci/run_bench.sh --job nightly --model model-optim --gpus 4 --seq 2048 --batch 1` and then monitor `pmap`/`smem`. If you can get a pprof profile that'd be ideal: start with `PYTHONMALLOC=debug` and `--profile=mem`.

sam: also add `--disable-prefix-cache` as a quick toggle to rule out prefix/KV leak. If that avoids the spike, it's likely cache growth.

maria: i pulled the core and heaptrack from artifacts (linked). quick grep shows many allocations from `runtime::kv::insert` in the flame-graph. not definitive but suspicious.

kevin: ok that matches the RSS jump timing. can someone run `./tools/heap_diff` on the artifacts? I'm AFK for ~20m otherwise i'd do it.

jen: running repro now, will post pprof link when done. If this repros locally I'll bisect between HEAD and the allocator PR.

ops-oncall: adding oncall to the thread — @ops-oncall we might need a high-priority job slot for a bisect run, requesting 2h on a 32G GPU node.

ops-oncall: granted. reserved `ci-bisect-1995` node for the next 2h. please tag me when starting.

alex: plan: (1) jen to repro and generate mem profile (2) if repro succeeds, sam to run git-bisect local between HEAD and allocator PR (3) create a Jira (INF-1123) to track root cause and rollback if bisect points to allocator.

sam: noted. if bisect points to allocator opt i'll prepare a revert PR and smoke-test.

maria: quick find: one test-run showed `std::vector` growth with missing dealloc path in `kv::batch_update` when `prefetch=true`. could be a regression from the prefetch change.

jen: repro finished — attaching memprofile: https://ci.example/artifacts/1995032100/prof.heap. I toggled `--disable-prefix-cache` and spike went away. repro with cache on reproduces the OOM.

alex: that is a strong signal — cache/prefetch path. sam/maria can you bisect on code touching `kv` and prefetch?

sam: starting bisect now. will post commits checked and result. ETA ~45m.

kevin: while bisect runs, recommend creating a temporary mitigation: fail-safe to cap cache size per-request or trigger early eviction on large sequences. low-risk change to hotfix for nightly until root cause fixed.

alex: agree. let's push a quick mitigation PR with a conservative cache cap and enable only in nightly for now. assign to @sam for review.

maria: created Jira INF-1123 and added notes + artifacts + mitigation proposal. link: https://jira.example/browse/INF-1123

sam: bisect result: commit 3f7a9b2 introduced the regression — it is the `prefetch` change in kv that I suspected. I'll open PR to revert the prefetch portion and include tests.

jen: i'll run the nightly job with the revert locally and report back.

ops-oncall: logging all actions in incident channel for visibility and marking as P2. if revert lands, i'll run an extended nightly to validate.

alex: perfect. thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the coordination point. follow-ups: PR link, CI rerun, and postmortem draft once root cause confirmed. :thumbsup:

sam: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/799 (revert prefetch tweak) — cc: @maria @alex

jen: local validation looks good, no OOM after revert. will queue the extended run on `ci-bisect-1995`.

maria: adding test case to cover large-seq eviction path so we don't regress again.

alex: closing loop — we'll keep the mitigation until postmortem and tests land. tagging INF-1123 as in-progress. thanks all.
